name: discover-layer-data-constraints-full
description: The `data_constraints` layer's descriptor at `form: "full"` — the one form that carries the descriptor PROSE, asked for one layer at a time because the project-wide `full` discovery is REFUSED with `over-budget` on every project (`negative/discover-project-full-over-budget.json`), and the refusal's second step is exactly this request. Together the fifteen per-layer `full` vectors replay every layer, kind and field annotation the model contract ships, verbatim, which is where the shipped-prose oracle (`packages/tools/tests/test_model_contract_conformance.py`) rides: rewording an annotation in the contract is a protocol-output change, and this is the output it changes. Of this layer: the `data_constraints` layer contract `8.0.0` added for the physical limits a type names by reference, stored in `data_types/constraints/`, with exactly one kind, `data_constr`, and therefore no discriminator. An application type's `data_constr_ref` is resolved in this layer alone.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` shape of a SWCraft project: fifteen scaffolded layers, `data_constraints` among them and empty in `data_types/constraints/`. Nothing about the response depends on which elements are in the layer: the inventory is derived from the model contract through the registry, not from the files.

layers.description: Data constraints, one file each under `data_types/constraints/`: the physical limits a value is declared within, an element a type names by reference. One kind, `data_constr`, which an application type names as its `data_constr_ref`. The directory is mandatory and may be empty.

element_kinds.description: A data constraint, emitted as a `DATA-CONSTR` in `/DataTypes/Constraints` with one rule of `PHYS-CONSTRS`: the physical limits an application type is declared within. An application type names one by its `data_constr_ref`, in place of an inline `range`. It holds no internal limits.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The data constraint's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/constraints/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the data constraints, must not be blank, and immutable; an element of another layer may carry the same name.

fields.name: min
fields.description: The lower physical limit; omitted or `null` when there is none. An integer is held as the integer it is; NaN and ±Infinity are refused.

fields.name: max
fields.description: The upper physical limit; omitted or `null` when there is none. An integer is held as the integer it is; NaN and ±Infinity are refused.

fields.name: level
fields.description: The rule's `CONSTR-LEVEL`, the category of the constraint (the lower the level, the more stringent the check); omitted or `null` when the rule states none.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free text about the data constraint. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

fields.name: package
fields.description: The one sub-package of `/DataTypes/Constraints`, its layer's package, this data constraint is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the data constraint and every reference to it take `/DataTypes/Constraints/{package}/`. Absent means `/DataTypes/Constraints` itself. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule.

expected.notes: The same document the default form answers with `description` restored on the layer, on every kind and on every field that declares one, and with the three descriptor booleans spelled out where the default form omits them at `false` — `optional` on the layer, `required` and `immutable` on every field. Nothing else is restored, because nothing else is left out. `baseline` is the stand-in token every vector carries; a harness replaces it with the project's own.
